Capacious

kuh-PAY-shus · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Capacious is having a great deal of space inside; roomy.

The capacious lecture hall could seat the entire freshman class with room to spare.

Worked Example

Her capacious handbag somehow held an umbrella, a laptop, two books, and a full lunch.

Capacious specifically emphasizes generous interior space for holding or containing things.

How Capacious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

roomy

roomy: the everyday word for having plenty of space; capacious is its formal counterpart for generous room inside

spacious

spacious: having a lot of available space

Antonyms

cramped

cramped: uncomfortably small

confined

confined: restricted in space

How Strong Is It? — big → capacious → cavernous

big vs. capacious

big vs. capacious: Big is a plain, general word for size; capacious specifically emphasizes generous interior space for holding things.

cavernous vs. capacious

cavernous vs. capacious: Cavernous goes further than capacious, describing a space so vast it feels like a cave.

The pieces

root — capac

root — capac: able to hold (Latin (capere, capax))

suffix — -ious

suffix — -ious: full of, characterized by (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: capac- ('able to hold') + -ious together describe something able to hold a great deal.
